cheng: Heads up 1: prototyping a tenant-local control-plane option for small customers. Goal: better isolation and lower cross-tenant blast radius. Main open items: DNS handoff model, certificate rotation throughput, and a minimal fallback proxy for sidecarless apps. Thoughts? :eyes:

alex: nice. two quick clarifications: are we doing full NS delegation (customer zone delegated to tenant CP) or split DNS (redwood conditionally forwards)? each has different outage modes.

maria: NS delegation gives the clearest ownership but has a slow propagation window. For certs we need to ensure rotation doesn't spam customer KMS. Batch and coalesce is mandatory.

sanjay: agree. propose a per-region batched rotation queue with a token-bucket limiter per-tenant. default batch window 45s, token refill 10 ops/sec, tunable. reduces KMS HSM hot paths.

cheng: good. alex: if delegation is NS, how do we detect partial delegation (some resolvers still hit our apex)? need a fallback plan.

alex: detection: probe from multiple public resolvers and our internal probes; if mismatch for >2 minutes mark "partial-delegate". Fallback: serve synthetic DNS records from redwood for a short TTL (5m) while we wait for glue to settle.

kirby: synthetic DNS is fine but must be scoped: only answer A/AAAA for endpoint records, never give MX/other sensitive records. Also add strict TTL controls so rollback is fast.

maria: for cert controller API, sketch below: endpoints are very small set: POST /rotate, GET /status, GET /metrics. Payload minimal, controller groups by (tenant_id, region), returns op id. Batching: controller waits up to batch_window or until batch_size reached.

cheng: sample request?
maria: ```
POST /v1/tenants/{tid}/cert-ops
{
  "op": "rotate",
  "kind": "leaf",
  "priority": "normal",
  "requested_at": "2026-03-23T15:00:00Z"
}
```async op id returned. controller aggregates operations and makes single KMS call where possible (use envelope keys to share unwrap).

alex: important: some customers require an allowlist step before we bring new cert live. we need a "activate_after_whitelist" flag. If set, rotation pauses until customer confirms fingerprint.

sanjay: then rotation controller needs two code paths: auto-activate and manual-approval. For manual, we emit a webhook/event and set tenant state to waiting_for_whitelist. Implement retry/backoff for webhooks.

kirby: operationally: add KMS throttling in front of batch executor. If KMS errors > 3% for 2m, pause new batches and create ticket/alert to secops. Also add a circuit breaker to fail open with degrade mode where existing certs remain valid longer.

maria: metrics we should track: cert_batches_total, avg_batch_latency_seconds, kms_errors, pending_manual_approvals, dns_partial_delegate_events. Also expose batch_size histogram.

cheng: rollback semantics? if delegation partially applied and we already flipped CP weight, customers could see split responses. We should adopt blue/green activation with weight markers and health gating.

sanjay: concrete flow: 1) provision tenant CP (green) with weight=0, 2) push delegation/glue, 3) wait for probe consensus (>=90% resolvers agree), 4) health probes pass >=95% for 3 polls, 5) set weight->100. If step 3 or 4 fails, set weight->0 and revoke delegation attempt. All flips are idempotent.

alex: include CLI snippets in runbook:
```
redwoodctl cp create --tenant $T --region us-west-2 --type tenant-local
redwoodctl dns delegate --zone example.com --ns ns1.cp.example.net
redwoodctl cp set-weight --tenant $T --cp $ID --weight 0
# wait for probes
redwoodctl cp set-weight --tenant $T --cp $ID --weight 100
```

cheng: good. one more debate: mTLS termination location. Options: terminate in tenant CP and supply short-lived client certs to dataplane, or terminate in a tiny proxy in-customer network (sidecar). Sidecarless customers prefer no sidecar but that complicates client cert distribution.

maria: recommend hybrid: default to tenant CP termination with a lightweight proxy (redistributable binary) as optional for legacy networks. The proxy only performs TLS handshake and health checks, not routing.

kirby: add runbook steps: pre-checks before delegation (zone lock present, glue applied), KMS quota check, cert-controller health, synthetic-dns toggle. Add automated checklist that fails fast if any pre-check fails.

sanjay: also add a safety throttle: per-org concurrent delegations <= 5 by default, can be increased after monitoring. This avoids large-scale DNS churn.
